notes: 50 states + DC + PR. PR is included because zip_crosswalk.json already resolves 132 PR ZIPs, so excluding it would leave those ZIPs unable to join. No lender serves PR, so a PR ZIP correctly returns zero results rather than an error.
Full name for display. "220 lenders licensed in Florida" reads better than "in FL".
Joins to the first two digits of any county GEOID.

GEOID = state FIPS + county FIPS. This must be the key, not the name: county names repeat heavily across states (30+ states have a Washington County). Our ZIP crosswalk stores names only, giving just 1956 distinct names for 3222 counties. 3230 rows = 3222 current + 8 retired CT counties.
Full legal name with suffix: "Palm Beach County", "Orleans Parish", "Anchorage Municipality". Suffix varies by state — do not assume "County". CT uses "Planning Region" and DC has no suffix.

Suffix stripped ("Palm Beach"). Normalises cash_buyers.coverage[], which stores bare names. NOT unique, even within a state: MD has Baltimore County and Baltimore city, MO has the St. Louis pair, VA has four. A name-only lookup is genuinely ambiguous and can return 2 rows.
Indexed with lower(short_name). No FK yet — geo_state does not exist. One FIPS prefix per state, so fips[:2] is a reliable state key.
False for the 8 retired CT counties. Filter on this for pickers and dropdowns; leave it out when resolving a FIPS that came from stored data, or older records dangle.
Gazetteer INTPTLAT. Null only for retired rows. Aleutians West (02016) crosses the antimeridian, so its lng is positive — do not assume a negative longitude.
Gazetteer INTPTLONG. Null only for retired rows.

Built from Census places, NOT HUD as this spec originally proposed. The driving requirement turned out to be resolving cash_buyers.coverage[] city names to counties, and the Census place file carries a COUNTIES field that states the answer outright; HUD would have required deriving it through ZIPs. Revisit HUD only if USPS-preferred names are needed for address display. State FIPS + place FIPS.
Full legal name including governmental type: "Tampa city", "Nashville-Davidson metropolitan government (balance)".
Governmental type stripped ("Tampa"). NOT unique within a state — TX has two Springfields in different counties, which resolve as ambiguous rather than being guessed.

Alternate names pulled out of parentheticals and city-county consolidations: "El Paso de Robles (Paso Robles)" yields "Paso Robles", "Nashville-Davidson metropolitan government (balance)" yields "Nashville". Without this the largest consolidated cities are unsearchable. GIN indexed.
Indexed with lower(short_name). Every lookup is state-scoped — an unscoped city name is not resolvable.

An ARRAY, not the single primary_county_fips this spec first proposed. Places genuinely straddle counties — Kansas City MO sits in four — and picking the largest would silently drop the rest. GIN indexed. FIPS are resolved against geo_counties at build time; places whose counties do not resolve (US territories) are dropped.
Already built and in production. Leading zeros are significant — keep as text, never integer.
100% populated. Border ZIPs already resolved to the USPS state rather than largest land area.
The single missing piece. Everything else about ZIPs is already solved.
We have the county NAME for 33774 of 42570 ZIPs; converting to FIPS is a join, not new data. The 8796 without a county are PO-box and single-point ZIPs with no Census ZCTA — leave null, never infer.
Optional until radius search exists.
Optional until radius search exists.
Many-to-many: 10092 ZIPs touch more than one county. A single county column would silently drop coverage for those.
FK to geo_county. PRIMARY KEY (zip, county_fips).
Largest land-area part. Used for display; matching should consider every row.

THE source for USPS city names. Free, requires a registered token. Bearer auth. type=2 (zip-county), query=All returns the whole file. Fields USPS_ZIP_PREF_CITY / USPS_ZIP_PREF_STATE. Updated quarterly. Authoritative and covers all USPS ZIPs.
142 KB zip. Fields: USPS, GEOID, NAME, ALAND, INTPTLAT, INTPTLONG. File is UTF-8 — decoding as latin-1 corrupts "Doña Ana County". Rebuild via backend/scripts/build_counties_data.py.
1.2 MB zip. Not used: the Gazetteer place file has coordinates but no county column, so it cannot answer "which county is this city in?". The national place file below can.

national_place2020.txt. Carries a COUNTIES field naming every county a place sits in — the field that makes buyer coverage matching possible. Pipe-delimited, latin-1. Rebuild via backend/scripts/build_cities_data.py, seed via scripts/seed_geo_cities.py.
6.8 MB. Already powers zip_crosswalk.json via backend/scripts/build_zip_crosswalk.py.

CC BY 4.0 but requires a visible backlink on a public page before production use. Only 33782 ZIPs (ZCTAs only) — misses the same 8796 USPS-only ZIPs we already had to patch. Weaker than HUD for our case.
All USPS ZIPs, no attribution, no redistribution permitted. Buys convenience over HUD, not coverage. 12 months of updates.

Already carries geoid + county + state + state_full for 3216 counties (6 short of the gazetteer's 3222). Stores SHORT names ("Autauga") where the gazetteer stores full ("Autauga County"). Seed geo_county from the gazetteer and leave this file alone — it is load-bearing for insurance estimates.

zip_crosswalk.json is already 1.4 MB loaded per worker process. Adding cities plus fuzzy autocomplete exceeds what a JSON file should carry. Needs pg_trgm indexes on geo_city.name and geo_city_alias.alias.

CT replaced its 8 county governments with 9 planning regions in 2022. The 2024 Gazetteer lists the regions; zip_crosswalk.json (2020 ZCTA vintage) still names the old counties for 445 CT ZIPs. geo_counties carries both vintages, so all 3221 (state,county) pairs the crosswalk references now resolve — it was 86 unresolved before (78 PR + 8 CT). Pinned by test_every_county_named_by_the_zip_crosswalk_resolves.
A geo database says which counties exist. It cannot say which counties a lender will lend in. Lender county filtering still depends entirely on counties_served in the regenerated lender dataset.

app/services/geo_matching.py is the only code that interprets a coverage string. The backfill and scripts/report_buyer_coverage_gaps.py both call it, so coverage-unmatched.csv is exactly the set of strings that did not become directory_service_area rows. Name folding is done in Python, not SQL, so the read path cannot fold differently from the write path.

90.6% of 9871 strings resolve (87.1% to counties, 3.4% state-wide, 0.1% nationwide). Counties alone reached 59.6%; geo_cities plus suffix/punctuation handling closed the gap. The residual 9.3% would require guessing: buyers with no state on record, counties in a neighbouring state (a Memphis buyer covering "DeSoto", which is in Mississippi), and metro nicknames with no legal geography ("Hampton Roads").
